verdict: Zoetis revenue slipped 1% to $2.4B as U.S. companion-animal sales fell on dermatology competition and price sensitivity, partly offset by livestock growth and a 4% rise internationally — and GAAP profit fell 18%.

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: +3% vs a year ago, excluding one-off items

kpis.label: U.S. revenue
kpis.note: -6% vs a year ago — the weak spot of the quarter

segments.name: United States
segments.note: Zoetis's home market. Companion-animal revenue fell 8% on dermatology competition, generic pressure and price sensitivity, while livestock revenue rose 5%.

segments.name: International
segments.note: All markets outside the U.S. Companion-animal revenue rose 1% and livestock revenue rose 8%.

segments.name: Contract Manufacturing & Human Health
segments.note: Contract manufacturing for others (Client Supply Services) plus the human-health business — small, and not part of either geographic segment.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: The sales force that calls on vets and livestock producers, plus head-office costs.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new animal medicines, vaccines and diagnostics.

opex.name: Restructuring and certain acquisition/divestiture costs
opex.note: Restructuring charges plus certain acquisition and divestiture-related costs — up from just $4M a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down product rights and other intangibles bought in past deals, year by year.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $62M plus $72M of other deductions—net — a year ago that second line was $12M of income, so the swing cost about $84M year over year.
oneTimers: Restructuring charges and certain acquisition/divestiture-related costs jumped to $43M from $4M a year ago.

Adjusted net income of $720M excludes a net $129M impact from purchase-accounting adjustments, acquisition and divestiture-related costs and certain significant items — which is why adjusted EPS rose 3% while GAAP EPS fell 12%.
The divested medicated feed additive portfolio cut revenue growth by about 1 percentage point in the quarter.

takeaways.title: U.S. pet products are the problem
takeaways.text: U.S. companion-animal revenue fell 8% as dermatology products faced competition and pet owners showed price sensitivity. U.S. livestock rose 5%, cushioning the segment's 6% decline.

takeaways.title: International and livestock grew
takeaways.text: International revenue rose 4% to $1,116M and worldwide livestock revenue rose 7% to $797M, offsetting much of the U.S. pet weakness.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS still rose
takeaways.text: GAAP net income fell 18% to $591M on higher restructuring and other deductions, but adjusted EPS rose 3% to $1.75 — and Zoetis raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance while narrowing its revenue guidance.

footerNote: Zoetis does not print an operating-income subtotal — it lists interest expense and other deductions among its costs and expenses. Operating income here ($863M) is gross profit less SG&A, R&D, amortization and restructuring charges, with the $62M of interest and $72M of other deductions shown below it in Other income. Segment figures are the printed U.S., International and Contract Manufacturing & Human Health revenues from the release.
